summary: Your neighbors pick a leader: At {local group}'s meeting, {member} nominates you out loud to lead it.
realLife: In 1832, about a year after moving to New Salem, Illinois, his neighbors elected him captain of their militia company. He lost his legislative race that year but carried New Salem almost to a man.
gates: You belong to {local group} and its leader post is open.
choices: accept only if someone you trust takes the second spot

branches.when: the group must take a side
branches.then: Soon it has to back or oppose a ballot measure or a candidate, and as its leader you speak for it.
The vote is by hands, and the loser is someone you see every week.

branches.when: only your own street backs you
branches.then: The tally shows where your support lives, which a later race reads.
